note: Each case: verify `bundle` with the named keys (see `keys`) and, when `log` is not null, a copy of the log whose lines are these leaves. `expected.failing` lists the check names that must fail; `expected.ok` is true only when it is empty.

cases.name: gateway-executed
cases.description: An in-policy refund through the gateway: delegation attested, facts observed, executed. Every check passes with the log.

cases.name: gateway-executed-proto-key
cases.description: The call's arguments carry an own property named __proto__. The receipt records it and the args digest covers it (a canonicaliser that loses the key fails the digest check).

cases.name: gateway-private-clear-result-upstream-attested
cases.description: A refund whose arguments are withheld (digest) and whose result the rule leaves in clear. The result's _meta is withheld, as it always is under a private rule, and the upstream's plain attestation stays in clear beside the result. With the upstream key given, `upstream signature (upstream key)` runs and passes in both verifiers: the signature covers the content and isError, never _meta. The expected outcome alone cannot tell a pass from a skip; the wrong-key case beside it shows the check runs.

cases.name: gateway-private-clear-result-upstream-wrong-key
cases.description: The same receipt with the principal's key offered as the upstream key. The check runs rather than being skipped for the withheld _meta, so `upstream signature (upstream key)` fails in both verifiers; everything else passes.

cases.name: gateway-executed-private
cases.description: A refund whose capture rule withholds the note (encrypted), the provider's answer (digest), and the customer record (encrypted): the receipt carries commitments, the digests are over the whole call, and without the key or a disclosure the verifier passes them as committed, not recomputed, and does not check the upstream's signature.

cases.name: sdk-malformed-commitment-resigned
cases.description: An SDK receipt whose request argument is replaced by `{ $custody: "withheld" }` with no sha256 and no salt, a capture note naming that path added, the original digest kept, re-signed. A tag without the fields a verifier checks is not a commitment, so the note is not borne out and the args digest check fails in both verifiers.

cases.name: sdk-array-hash-commitment-resigned
cases.description: As above, with `sha256` an array holding one well-formed hash instead of a string. A pattern test that coerces its argument would take it for a commitment; both verifiers require a string, and the args digest check fails.

cases.name: sdk-array-keyid-commitment-resigned
cases.description: An encrypted-shaped commitment whose `keyid` is an array holding one hex string. Not a commitment in either verifier; the args digest check fails.

cases.name: gateway-undeclared-envelope-commitment-resigned
cases.description: An executed receipt with a clear result whose upstream envelope is replaced by a well-formed commitment, with no capture note naming it, re-signed. The note, not the shape, says what is withheld: with the upstream key given, the signature check fails instead of being skipped.

cases.name: resigned-status-withheld
cases.description: The executed receipt's execution.status replaced by a well-formed commitment, named in the note, re-signed. A note may not name what a verifier reads to run its checks: the statement fails `structural parts in clear` in both verifiers.

cases.name: resigned-tool-withheld
cases.description: The whole `tool` replaced by a commitment and named in the note. Fails `structural parts in clear`.

cases.name: resigned-delegation-withheld
cases.description: The grant replaced by a commitment and named in the note. Fails `structural parts in clear` rather than throwing.

cases.name: resigned-note-malformed
cases.description: A capture note that is a number. Fails `structural parts in clear` in both verifiers, the same way.

cases.name: resigned-note-path-twice
cases.description: A capture note naming the same path twice. No issuer writes one; fails `structural parts in clear` in both verifiers.

cases.name: resigned-note-path-proto
cases.description: A capture note whose path begins with __proto__. A lookup of that head in an ordinary object would throw; both verifiers fail `structural parts in clear` instead.

cases.name: resigned-clear-result-envelope-withheld
cases.description: The executed receipt with its result in clear and its upstream envelope replaced by a digest-only commitment named in the note, re-signed. A withheld signature beside a result in clear is not a reason to skip the check: with the upstream key given, `upstream signature (upstream key)` fails in both verifiers.

cases.name: resigned-note-path-string
cases.description: A capture note whose path is a string rather than segments. Fails `structural parts in clear` in both verifiers, the same way.

cases.name: resigned-policy-no-digest
cases.description: The executed receipt's policy without `policyDigest`, re-signed. The spec requires the digest of the policy text; both verifiers fail `structural parts in clear` instead of throwing.

cases.name: resigned-principal-no-keyid
cases.description: The executed receipt's attested principal without `keyid`, re-signed. The spec gives an attested principal a key id; both verifiers fail `structural parts in clear` instead of throwing.

cases.name: gateway-private-short-tag-resigned
cases.description: The private receipt's encrypted commitment over the arguments with its tag cut to 4 bytes, re-signed with the gateway key. A tag shorter than 16 bytes is not a commitment in either verifier, so the note is not borne out and the args digest check fails.

cases.name: sdk-custody-shaped-data-resigned
cases.description: An SDK receipt whose result carries data shaped like a commitment but no capture note, with the result edited and re-signed. The data is ordinary, the digest covers it, and the result digest check fails: a verifier must not skip a digest on the shape of the data.

cases.name: gateway-denied-expired-grant
cases.description: The session's grant expired before this call; the gateway denied it and issued the receipt after the window. Denied, so the validity check passes with a note; an executed receipt timestamped outside the window would not.

cases.name: gateway-denied
cases.description: An over-limit refund denied by policy. The receipt exists, execution is denied, and every check passes.

cases.name: gateway-executed-upstream-attested
cases.description: The executed receipt verified with the upstream's key as well: the upstream signed its result for this receipt, so the execution is attested, not only observed.

cases.name: gateway-executed-upstream-wrong-key
cases.description: The same receipt with the principal's key offered as the upstream key. The upstream signature check fails; everything else passes.

cases.name: gateway-executed-no-log-copy
cases.description: The same executed receipt verified without a copy of the log: inclusion still proven against the signed tree head, the log-file check simply absent.

cases.name: wrong-issuer-key
cases.description: Verified against the principal's key as if it were the issuer's. The signature check fails first and nothing else is decided.

cases.name: tampered-payload
cases.description: One character of the base64 payload changed. The signature no longer verifies.

cases.name: resigned-tool-out-of-scope
cases.description: Predicate edited to name a tool outside the grant, then re-signed with the real gateway key. The signature passes; the scope check fails; the log no longer contains this leaf.

cases.name: resigned-policy-inconsistent
cases.description: Predicate edited so the policy says deny while execution says executed, re-signed with the gateway key.

cases.name: resigned-args-digest
cases.description: Request args edited without updating the digest, re-signed with the gateway key.

cases.name: resigned-body-note-without-commitment
cases.description: The executed receipt's capture note says the provider's delivery body is withheld, the evidence is removed, the result edited, re-signed with the gateway key. A note naming a path the receipt carries no commitment for fails that path's check in both verifiers, and the edited result fails its digest.

cases.name: resigned-result-digest
cases.description: Execution result edited without updating the result digest, re-signed with the gateway key. The result digest check fails.

cases.name: inclusion-proof-wrong-index
cases.description: The inclusion proof's leaf index changed. The tree head still verifies; the proof does not.

cases.name: log-copy-from-another-log
cases.description: Verified against a copy of a different log. Everything passes except the recomputed root.

failing: log file root matches tree head

cases.name: gateway-chain-executed
cases.description: A refund by a sub-agent under a two-link delegation chain: the principal granted the planner, whose key the grant names; the planner delegated the refund to the refunder. The chain verifies to the principal's key, the receipt names the refunder and the principal, and every check passes.

cases.name: gateway-chain-offset-window-resigned
cases.description: The chain's leaf re-issued with a start time written in a +02:00 offset: as text it sorts after the parent's start, as an instant it is an hour before it. Both verifiers must compare instants and refuse the link; the re-signed receipt also loses its inclusion.

cases.name: gateway-chain-escalated-resigned
cases.description: The same receipt with the chain's leaf replaced by one giving the refunder a scope the planner never held, signed with the planner's real key, then the receipt re-signed with the gateway key. The chain check fails on that link; the re-signed receipt also loses its inclusion.

cases.name: gateway-observe-denied
cases.description: The over-limit refund through a gateway in observe mode: the policy says deny, the call was forwarded anyway, and the receipt carries enforced: false. Every check passes; the consistency check names the mode.

cases.name: resigned-observe-flag-stripped
cases.description: The same receipt with enforced: false removed and re-signed with the gateway key: a deny now claims to have been enforced beside an executed call, and the consistency check fails.

cases.name: gateway-precommit-executed
cases.description: A consequential refund: the gateway committed a signed authorization to the log before forwarding the call, and the receipt embeds it. The five authorization checks pass, and the authorization leaf precedes the receipt leaf.

cases.name: gateway-precommit-spliced
cases.description: The second refund's receipt carrying the first refund's authorization, re-signed with the gateway key. The authorization verifies as a statement but does not name this call; the re-signed receipt also loses its own inclusion.

cases.name: gateway-precommit-reordered
cases.description: The authorization's inclusion proof replaced by the receipt's own, so it claims a leaf after the execution. The proof fails and so does the order check.

cases.name: resigned-authorization-no-inclusion
cases.description: The committed receipt's authorization without its `inclusion` proof, re-signed. The spec gives an authorization an envelope, a tree head, and a proof; both verifiers fail `structural parts in clear` instead of throwing.

cases.name: resigned-authorization-no-tree-head
cases.description: The committed receipt's authorization without its `treeHead`, re-signed. Fails `structural parts in clear` in both verifiers.

cases.name: gateway-executed-stripe-webhook
cases.description: The upstream attached the Stripe webhook for the refund, signed with the shared secret whsec_vectors. With that secret given, the delivery verifies and binds to the refund id in the result: attested by shared secret.

cases.name: resigned-provider-bound-value-missing
cases.description: The webhook receipt with the result's content replaced (the refund id gone), the result digest recomputed, the metadata copy of the delivery kept, re-signed. The delivery's bound value must appear in what the agent received, never in the delivery's own copy in the metadata: the provider check fails.

cases.name: gateway-executed-stripe-webhook-wrong-secret
cases.description: The same receipt with the wrong secret. The provider check fails; everything else passes.

cases.name: gateway-executed-stripe-webhook-no-secret
cases.description: The same receipt with no secret given. The delivery is carried, not checked; every other check passes.

cases.name: sdk-executed
cases.description: A receipt from the in-process SDK: issuer kind sdk, principal claimed, no delegation, every field claimed. Passes; the report says what it is worth.

cases.name: sdk-denied
cases.description: An SDK denial receipt: the wrapped function was never called.

cases.name: remote-log-with-log-key
cases.description: Logged to a log run by someone else: the tree head is signed by the log's key. With that key trusted, everything passes and the report names the log key.

cases.name: remote-log-expected-id
cases.description: The same receipt with the expected log id given. The tree head names vectors-log, so the check passes; the log file is hash-only and its root still matches.

cases.name: remote-log-wrong-id
cases.description: The same receipt with a different expected log id. Only the log-id check fails.

failing: tree head names the expected log

cases.name: remote-log-without-log-key
cases.description: The same receipt with only the issuer key trusted. The tree head signature fails; nothing about inclusion can be decided.

cases.name: financial-unknown
cases.description: Provider accepted a refund but its response was lost. The operation is unknown, its budget stays reserved, and its committed authorization verifies.

cases.name: financial-reconciled
cases.description: An observed provider read closes the unknown operation as confirmed. Original identity, precommitted lookup mapping, provider idempotency key, result digest and log order all verify.

cases.name: financial-wrong-operation
cases.description: A re-signed reconciliation whose operation id differs from the embedded original.

cases.name: financial-remapped-provider-state
cases.description: A re-signed reconciliation changes the terminal provider mapping after authorization.

cases.name: financial-unrelated-provider-record
cases.description: The issuer re-signs a provider result carrying another idempotency key, recomputing the result digest. The provider status check still fails.
